newsitem.title: USA: US OPTIONS FOCUS/Index traders look to next week.
newsitem.headline: US OPTIONS FOCUS/Index traders look to next week.

text.p: Activity in major U.S. stock index options remained under wraps Thursday as investors had few incentives to be aggressive on either the long or the short side, traders said.

One S&P 500 index .SPX options trader said several institutions on Wednesday had been actively buying and selling combinations in June, September and December expirations, but that activity had died down by Thursday.
"I don't think the (trading) pit's expecting anything until later next week," he said. "That's the consensus."
The May U.S. jobless report is scheduled for release on June 6.
"We're in for a slow week," said an SPX futures-options trader at the Chicago Mercantile Exchange, explaining that activity should be quiet up to the employment report.
He added that volatilities in the June series were fairly flat from Wednesday levels.
Another SPX futures-options trader said volatility in the June series had moved around since Wednesday morning but had come back to the 18.4 percent level seen Wednesday morning.
At the Chicago Board Options Exchange, where SPX options trade, "nothing's really coming out of volatility except for normal time decay," the SPX trader said.
In the S&P 100 index .OEX, volatility as measured by the volatility index .VIX, which is calculated off certain OEX options contracts, was up 0.04 at 21.67 in afternoon activity.
The spot OEX was down 2.62 at 828.68 and the spot SPX was off 2.06 at 845.15. June S&P 500 futures lost 3.35 to 847.20.
One firm had pegged June S&P 500 fair value at two points premium to cash, with buy programs at 3.50 points over or wider and sell programs at 0.80 points over or narrower.
SPX futures-options traders said large dealers were actively buying July call spreads out of the money, particularly the 895/910 call spread.
One firm was also seen selling some June call spreads.
"A lot of people are looking at the market," one trader said. "There are a lot of buyers of upside call spreads and sellers of downside September puts."
He added that one overseas financial house was an aggressive seller of some September puts.
